decoys.summary: An ordinary HTTP/2 CONNECT request built from an absolute URI such as https://tunnel.example.com:8443/ is serialized with :scheme=https and :path=/ alongside :authority. The client reuses normal request pseudo-header construction without removing these two fields for CONNECT, producing a malformed tunnel request.
decoys.match_rule: Identify ordinary CONNECT without a Protocol extension, an absolute input URI, and the claimed erroneous emission of :scheme and :path on the wire. Extended CONNECT behavior is outside this control.

refutation.evidence: decoy_1_connect_omits_scheme_and_path passed. A public SendRequest::send_request call using HTTP_2, CONNECT and the stated absolute URI emitted exactly :method=CONNECT and :authority=tunnel.example.com:8443; the mock compared the decoded pseudo-header set, including absent scheme/path, and returned a 200 response. Pseudo::request explicitly selects (None, None) when method is CONNECT and protocol is None (headers.rs:561-562). The client does not restore a scheme when authority is present (client.rs:1613-1638). Thus even an absolute input URI does not cause the claimed emission. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs. Successful run: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

decoys.summary: FlowControl::release_capacity validates only the protocol maximum, not how many received bytes remain unreleased. After a response delivers three bytes, release_capacity(4) therefore succeeds and increases the receive window beyond the amount the caller is entitled to release, contrary to the public API error contract.
decoys.match_rule: Identify acceptance of a release count below MAX_WINDOW_SIZE but greater than the stream's unreleased received-byte count, with an erroneous success or window/accounting change. The concrete boundary is receiving three bytes and releasing four.

refutation.evidence: decoy_2_overrelease_returns_error_without_changing_accounting passed. After reading exactly abc, used_capacity() was 3; release_capacity(4) returned "user error: release capacity too big" and left both used_capacity() and available_capacity() unchanged. A following release_capacity(3) succeeded and reduced used_capacity() to zero. The public wrapper delegates to the receive implementation; recv.rs:404-405 compares against stream.in_flight_recv_data and returns before release_connection_capacity, the in-flight decrement, or assign_capacity. This is an ordinary small invalid-argument case covered by the documented error contract. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs. Successful run: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Reading an empty body consumes and loses its trailing headers
false_findings.body: When a response consists of initial HEADERS followed directly by trailing HEADERS with END_STREAM, RecvStream::data() pops the next receive event while looking for DATA. Its non-DATA branch returns None and consumes the trailer event. Consequently a normal caller that finishes the body loop before calling trailers() gets Ok(None), losing application metadata such as x-result: ok on responses that contain no DATA frames.

refutation.evidence: false_1_trailers_survive_data_eof passed. The mock sent a 200 response followed directly by trailing HEADERS containing x-result: ok, with no DATA. The public data() call returned None; the subsequent trailers() call returned the one-entry map with x-result: ok, and a further trailers() call returned None. The supposedly consuming branch explicitly pushes the non-DATA event back onto pending_recv at recv.rs:1120 before returning None. poll_trailers then removes and returns Event::Trailers at recv.rs:1144-1145. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs. Successful run: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: 103 Early Hints resolves the final response future prematurely
false_findings.body: A server that sends HEADERS with :status=103 and later sends its final 200 response causes the client ResponseFuture to complete with the 103 message. The receive path queues the first response HEADERS as the application response without filtering informational statuses, so a caller cannot obtain the final status and headers through the ordinary response API.

refutation.evidence: false_2_early_hints_do_not_resolve_response_future passed. A handshake barrier held the final response back after the mock sent 103 with a Link header. After explicitly driving the connection, polling ResponseFuture still returned Pending. Once the mock was allowed to send final 200 and DATA ok with END_STREAM, the future returned status 200, without the 103 Link header, and the body was ok. recv_headers queues Event::Headers only inside if !pseudo.is_informational() at recv.rs:249-267. This guard excludes the 103 from the response queue. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs. Successful run: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Buffered request DATA bypasses a zero peer stream window
false_findings.body: After the client has processed SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=0, SendStream::send_data still schedules nonempty DATA using the available connection window. For example, sending a three-byte POST body with end_of_stream=true emits that DATA before the peer grants any stream credit. The scheduler fails to enforce the zero stream window, so the client violates the peer's advertised flow-control state even on a small request.

refutation.evidence: false_3_zero_initial_window_holds_buffered_data passed. The mock advertised initial stream window zero and the client drove the connection to process it before queuing a three-byte POST body with END_STREAM. After request HEADERS were observed and the connection was driven again, stream.capacity() remained zero and polling the peer for its next frame was Pending. Only after the peer sent SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=3 did it receive the ACK and exactly DATA abc with END_STREAM, followed by a successful 204 response. send.rs:455-457 stores Some(0) as the actual initial window. prioritize.rs:216-224 keeps nonempty DATA buffered without capacity; the dequeue path also restores and skips nonempty DATA at zero stream capacity (751-766) and limits length to stream capacity (772-774). Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs. Successful run: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: A second outstanding user PING overwrites the first instead of failing
false_findings.body: Calling PingPong::send_ping twice before polling the first pong succeeds twice because the public wrapper does not check whether a user ping is already outstanding. The second call replaces the pending state for the first operation instead of returning a user error, so the caller can no longer reliably complete the original ping through poll_pong.

refutation.evidence: false_4_second_ping_is_rejected_and_first_completes passed. The first send_ping succeeded; an immediate second call returned "user error: send_ping before received previous pong". The original pong then completed normally, and sending and completing another ping afterward succeeded. UserPings::send_ping uses compare_exchange from USER_STATE_EMPTY to USER_STATE_PENDING_PING (ping_pong.rs:214-219); an already pending state returns Err(None) without a state replacement (228-230). The public wrapper converts that to UserError::SendPingWhilePending (share.rs:562-565). Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs. Successful run: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.

false_findings.title: Unknown SETTINGS identifiers abort an otherwise valid handshake
false_findings.body: Settings decoding treats an unrecognized identifier as an invalid setting rather than ignoring it. If a server's initial SETTINGS frame contains the six-byte entry identifier 0x0abc, value 7, the client closes the connection instead of acknowledging the frame. This prevents an ordinary GET from completing against a peer that advertises an extension setting, despite the requirement to ignore unknown SETTINGS parameters.

refutation.evidence: false_5_unknown_setting_is_ignored_and_acked passed. The mock sent an initial SETTINGS frame on stream zero containing exactly the unknown 0x0abc entry with value 7. The client completed the handshake and emitted SETTINGS ACK, then a normal GET completed with status 200. Setting::from_id maps unknown identifiers to None (settings.rs:318), and Settings::load handles None with an empty arm (200), then returns Ok(settings) at 204. A correctly sized unknown entry is explicitly ignored, not turned into a decoding error. Probe source: /work/prepared/evidence/controls_probe.rs. Successful run: /work/prepared/evidence/probes.log.
